newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Wednesday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose to 1.496 billion yuan from 979 million on Tuesday and the 30-day contract was the most active.
Traders said trading volume recovered a little on Wednesday with the stock markets experiencing a technical rebound after sharp losses on Tuesday.
The stock markets plunged on Tuesday on rumours about the health of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, removing a major source of money demand from the interbank market.
Traders said both state banks and short-term financial centres, money brokerages run by the central bank, traded on Wedensday with a rise on the stock market pushing up demand.
"The rise of the stock markets was an important factor for the increase in interbank turnover today," said one trader.
The Finance Ministry announced on Tuesday that it would issue 123 billion yuan worth of two-, three- and five-year bonds from March 1 to October 20.
Traders said the issue would increase money demand on the interbank market, pushing up the rates in the mid-term.
Traders expect the rates to move in a narrow range on Thursday.
